location.evidence: Most top programs are in California, one of the best-paying states for mechanical engineers, or in Michigan, which employs more mechanical engineers than any other state. The bottom programs show no clear cluster.

prestige.evidence: The top programs admit far fewer applicants than the typical program, and MIT and Penn send graduates to top employers and graduate schools. The top ten also include less selective public schools in California and Michigan.

stepping_stone.evidence: Most new mechanical engineers go straight to full-time jobs. A smaller share continue to graduate study, as Penn Engineering's survey of its bachelor's graduates shows.

programs.evidence: Cal Maritime offers a license option within its mechanical engineering degree. Those students go to sea and must pass the Coast Guard exam for a Third Assistant Engineer license, which leads to work as a licensed marine engineer on ships.
MIT admits very few applicants. Its mechanical engineering graduates often go to top aerospace, automotive and energy firms or to leading graduate programs.
Penn is a highly selective school. Most of its engineering graduates take full-time jobs, many with large technology and industry employers, or go on to top graduate programs.
VMI says a large share of its graduates commission into the armed forces through ROTC. Many of its engineering graduates start as junior military officers, not civilian engineers.
Norwich is a senior military college, and many of its graduates commission into the armed services. Some engineering graduates start as junior officers, not civilian engineers.
Pay in Puerto Rico is far below mainland levels across all occupations. Engineering jobs on the island are few, so local graduates start at lower salaries.
